latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* Honor inverted Lightroom masks when importing catalog edits by @eliets2 in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3862
* LR-IMP-FORMATS: withdraw compressed ORF decoding pending provenance review by @FredApps in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3916
* Cover DxO demosaiced Fujifilm DNGs for Kelvin white balance by @eliets2 in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3887
* Release: refresh contributor credits for each release (#2254) by @Luis-0508 in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3898
* Issue #3776: one selected photo shows "1 selected" in the header by @ZIDAN44 in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3833
* Updates: the updater reports installing, ready, installed and failed, and installs at exit by @dotCooCoo in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3995
* Updates: take craft-update from craft-libs main at 1b34eba41 by @dotCooCoo in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3996
* LR-EDIT-EFFECTS-GRAIN: film grain from crystal layers (process V4), resolution independent, no GPU cost by @jeremyh in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3630

## New Contributors
* @Luis-0508 made their first contribution in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3898
* @ZIDAN44 made their first contribution in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3833
* @jeremyh made their first contribution in https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/3630

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/compare/v0.19.0...v0.20.0

detail.readme:
LightCraft

Your photos. Your pixels. Your machine.

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

Photo library and raw development; an open-source, non-destructive photo library and raw developer, built in pure Rust.
Native on macOS, Windows and Linux. In the browser via WebAssembly. Drivable end to end by AI agents over MCP.


LightCraft on getartcraft.com · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



Ansel Adams, "The Tetons and the Snake River" (1942). Public domain, U.S. National Archives. Developed in LightCraft.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Digital, generative, music, > games — if you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

Editing · Color grading · Before & after · Masking · Presets · Library · Agents & MCP · Performance · Status · Quick start · Roadmap · Downloads · Crafting Apps


## Edit like you mean it LightCraft is a complete darkroom in a single native app. Every adjustment is **non-destructive**, so your originals are never touched. Every slider renders through a **scene-referred, wide-gamut, 32-bit float pipeline**: highlights roll off like film, shadows open up without halos, and colour stays clean from capture to export.
### ☀️ Light **Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks**, with edge-aware local tone mapping (a guided filter on log-luminance). Pulling −100 Highlights recovers a blown sky without the grey halos you'd get from a naive curve. ### 🎨 Color **White balance** by temperature and tint (Kelvin for raw, relative for JPEG) with presets, Auto and a click-to-neutralise **eyedropper**. **Vibrance** that protects skin tones, **Saturation**, an 8-band **Color Mixer** (hue / saturation / luminance) and 3-way **Color Grading** wheels with blending and balance. All of it is computed in OkLCh, a modern perceptual colour space. ### ✨ Effects **Texture** for fine detail, **Clarity** for mid-tone punch, **Dehaze** (dark-channel prior with guided refinement; push it negative to add atmosphere), post-crop **Vignette** with highlight priority, roundness and feather, and resolution-independent film **Grain** with size and roughness. ### 📈 Tone Curve Parametric region curve with movable splits **plus** point curves for RGB, Red, Green and Blue. Curves are monotone by construction, so you never get an accidental tone inversion.


A gentle S on the RGB point curve, right under the Light sliders. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain).


## Color grading, the cinematic way Split-tone shadows, midtones and highlights independently with drag-anywhere colour wheels. Below, Dorothea Lange's *Migrant Mother* gets a warm, print-like tone (highlights at 42°, shadows at 28°) in two drags.


Shadows, midtones and highlights wheels in the Color panel. Dorothea Lange, "Migrant Mother" (1936). Public domain, Library of Congress.


## Before & after Press \\ to toggle the Before view, Y for side by side, or Shift+Y for a split view. Every image below is a real screenshot of LightCraft, captured automatically by an agent through the [control channel](#built-for-agents).

The Tetons and the Snake River. Highlights −45, Shadows +38, Clarity +28, Dehaze +18. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain).
Migrant Mother. Shadows +42, Texture +18, split-toned grade, vignette. Dorothea Lange, 1936 (public domain).

Earthrise. Dehaze +22, Highlights −30, warmer white balance, Vibrance +22. NASA / Bill Anders, Apollo 8, 1968 (public domain).
The Blue Marble. Highlights −38, Blacks −20, Dehaze +15, Vibrance +30. NASA, Apollo 17, 1972 (public domain).

## Masking that goes where you point Paint with a **Brush** (size, feather, flow, density, erase), drop **Linear** and **Radial Gradients** with draggable pins, or select by **Luminance Range**, **Color Range**, **Sky**, **Subject** and **Background**. Combine components with **Add / Subtract / Intersect**, invert any of them, and dial in 17 local adjustments per mask (Temp, Tint, Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Hue, Saturation, Sharpness, Noise, Moiré, Defringe), plus an overall Amount. Desktop **Object** and **Describe** masks use SAM 3 for click-based and text-prompt selection, with a separately installed model; see [model setup and terms](docs/ai-masks.md). Subject, Sky and Background selections still use classical heuristics. Existing model-generated masks render and export without the model installed.


A radial "Sun glow" mask (Temp +40, Exposure +0.50) layered over a linear "Sky" mask. Photo from LightCraft's procedurally generated demo library.


## Presets, profiles & the Color Mixer Forty-one hand-built presets ship in the box (*Golden Hour, Teal & Orange, Faded Matte, Selenium Tone, Crisp Landscape* and more), each with an **Amount** slider from 0 to 200 %. Save your own from any group of settings, mark favourites, and copy, paste or sync edits across a whole selection with exactly the groups you choose.


The Presets column next to the 8-band Color Mixer. Photo from the demo library.

### ✂️ Crop, straighten & geometry Free or locked aspect ratios (1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 4:3, 16:9, 16:10, original), drag-to-rotate straightening that always keeps the largest crop inside the image, thirds / grid / golden-ratio overlays, flips and 90° rotations, plus manual Vertical, Horizontal, Rotate, Aspect, Scale and Offset transforms. ### ⚫️ Black & White One click (V) to monochrome, with an 8-band **B&W Mix** that lets you darken skies or make foliage glow. Then tone it with Color Grading for selenium, sepia or split-tone prints.

A 16:9 crop straightened +2.5° with the thirds overlay. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain).
Split view: colour original on the left, B&W with Clarity, Vignette and Grain on the right. Demo library.

## Organize everything A library that stays out of your way: **All Photos**, **Recently Added**, **Picks**, **By Date**, **Albums** nested in **Folders**, and **Recently Deleted**. Rate with 0–5, flag with P / X / U, colour-label with 6–9. Search understands fields: `rating:>3 flag:pick iso:>800 camera:x2 date:2026-04 keyword:mountains person:"Jane Doe"`; plain words also match the people named on faces, and quotes keep several words together. Every view sorts by capture date, import date, edit date, name, rating, size or at random (a stable shuffle; View → Sort → Reshuffle for a new one). The justified **Photo Grid** and **Square Grid** views are virtualized, so they stay smooth whether you have forty photos or forty thousand. The **People** view groups named faces, including names read from XMP; face boxes can be edited in the loupe. On desktop, automatic detection and recognition use optional models installed through **Settings → Faces**; no weights are bundled. See [face models and setup](docs/faces.md).

Photo Grid with albums nested in a folder, ratings and flags. Demo library.
Square Grid of the four public-domain showcase photos.

The Info panel: file, dimensions, rating, title, caption, copyright and camera metadata. NASA / Bill Anders, "Earthrise", Apollo 8, 1968 (public domain).

## Built for agents Every menu item, slider, brush stroke, crop handle and keystroke in LightCraft is a **command** with a stable id and JSON parameters. The UI, the keyboard, the CLI, a JSON-lines control channel and an **MCP server** all dispatch through the same entry point. An agent can cull a shoot, develop it, mask a sky and export it, and *see* the result. ```sh lightcraft --control 7980 ~/Pictures/trip ``` ```jsonc {"method": "engine.execute", "params": {"command": "photo.flag", "params": {"flag": "pick"}}} {"method": "engine.execute", "params": {"command": "develop.set", "params": {"values": {"light.highlights": -45, "light.shadows": 38}}}} {"method": "engine.execute", "params": {"command": "mask.add", "params": {"kind": "radial", "center": [0.62, 0.4], "rx": 0.2, "ry": 0.14}}} {"method": "ui.clickWidget", "params": {"id": "slider:effects.clarity"}} // drive any widget by name {"method": "ui.pointer", "params": {"events": [{"kind":"down","x":0.2,"y":0.3}, {"kind":"up","x":0.4,"y":0.3}]}} {"method": "ui.screenshot", "params": {"path": "after.png"}} ``` - **Command registry.** `engine.commands` lists the available commands; `develop.controls` lists every slider's range, default and current value. - **MCP server.** `lightcraft-cli mcp` exposes the command registry to Claude (or any MCP client), alongside helpers for import, query, develop, render (returned as an image) and export. Masks have no helper of their own: create and edit them through `run_command` (e.g. `mask.add`). It runs headless, or attached to the running app with screenshots, clicks and gestures. See [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md). ```sh cargo build --release -p lightcraft-cli claude mcp add lightcraft -- "$PWD/target/release/lightcraft-cli" mcp ~/Pictures/shoot # headless claude mcp add lightcraft-app -- "$PWD/target/release/lightcraft-cli" mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7980 # live app ``` - **Scriptable CLI:** `lightcraft-cli run --import in.dng develop.set control=light.exposure value=0.7 app.export path=out.jpg longEdge=2048` runs any chain of commands (headless, on a saved library, or against the running app) and prints one JSON result per command; `lightcraft-cli render in.dng -o out.jpg --set light.exposure=0.7 --preset …`. - **Undo for everything**, including agent actions: a slider drag (or a scripted burst of updates) is one undo step. - **Contact sheets (native app / CLI):** select photos, then **File → Contact Sheet PDF…**. Choose A4 or Letter, landscape, rows/columns and filename captions; save a paginated PDF and print it from your PDF viewer. Exports use the current edits, fit each photo without further cropping, and render at 150 dpi in sRGB. The background export supports cancellation and protects originals and XMP sidecars. From the CLI: ```sh lightcraft-cli run --import ~/Pictures/shoot library.selectAll export.contactSheet path=Contact.pdf paper=a4 columns=3 rows=4 captions=true ``` `export.contactSheet` also accepts explicit `ids`, `landscape=true`, and `paper=letter`. It replaces an existing output only after the entire PDF succeeds. Limits: 1,000 photos, 100 pages, 256 MiB; captions are rasterized with the same font coverage as watermarks (CJK requires craft-fonts), with long names shortened in the middle. This is a contact-sheet workflow, not a printer-driver or custom picture-package layout editor. - **Print layouts (native app / CLI):** **File → Print…** opens the Print module's layout editor: Single Image, Contact Sheet, Picture Package (Auto Layout packs cells onto pages) and Custom Package (drag and resize cells, stacking order, snap to cells or a grid), Zoom to Fill / Rotate to Fit, Photo Border and Inner Stroke, paper sizes from 4 × 6 to 13 × 19 and A3 to A5 or custom, margins, rulers in in/cm/mm/pt, page background, 72–720 ppi, and saved templates. **Print to PDF…** renders in the background. Everything is a `print.*` command (`print.get`, `print.set`, `print.cell.add`, `print.layout.autoLayout`, `print.exportPdf`, `print.template.save`…), so the CLI and MCP drive it too: ```sh lightcraft-cli run --import ~/Pictures/shoot print.set 'layout={"style":"picturePackage","page":{"paper":"8x10"}}' \ print.cell.add width=5 height=7 print.cell.add width=2.5 height=3.5 print.layout.autoLayout print.exportPdf path=Package.pdf ``` The Print Job panel supports printer/paper ICC profiles, rendering intent, black point compensation, print adjustment, sharpening and 8/16-bit PDF output. Direct printing through an OS print dialog and page overlays (identity plate, watermark, page numbers) are not there yet. - **Slideshows:** **View → Slideshow** plays the photos in view full screen, with fades, repeat and random order. **Settings → Slideshow** configures layouts, templates, backgrounds, overlays and title screens. Native exports support PDF, JPEG sequences and AV1 video in MP4 or WebM; music and a dedicated Slideshow module editor remain missing. See [docs/slideshow.md](docs/slideshow.md). - **Every widget is addressable** (`ui.widgets`) and clickable by name, so agents operate the real UI, not a side door. - The screenshots in this README were produced end to end by the [`docs/showcase/`](docs/showcase/) scripts. Protocol reference: [docs/control-protocol.md](docs/control-protocol.md).
## Fast, native, private - **Pure Rust, no C.** Our own RAW decoders (DNG, Canon CR2/CR3, Sony ARW, Nikon NEF, Fujifilm RAF incl. X-Trans, Panasonic RW2 / Leica RWL, Pentax PEF, Olympus ORF), our own colour science, our own pipeline. JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, PSD composites, JPEG XL, GIF (first frame) and BMP open today; HEIC/HEIF photos too with `--features heif` (HEVC is a build-time choice, as in PhotoCraft). - **Scene-referred & wide-gamut.** Linear Rec.2020 float internally, Bradford-adapted white balance, gamut mapping instead of clipping, a filmic shoulder for raw and pixel-exact pass-through for JPEGs you haven't touched. - **Resolution-independent edits.** Radii and brush sizes are relative to the image, so a 400 px preview, your 5K display and a 60 MP export look the same. - **GPU-accelerated, CPU-exact.** The whole develop pipeline runs as wgpu compute kernels (Metal / Vulkan / DX12), checked against the CPU pipeline to within 1/255. On a 24 MP raw (Apple M4 Pro): a slider update re-renders in ~4 ms, a cold 2.5 MP loupe in ~30 ms, and a full-size export in ~0.3 s including a parallel JPEG encode. Without a GPU the same pipeline runs on all CPU cores, redoing only the stages a slider affects. Batch exports render several photos side by side, so one's decode and encode overlap another's render. - **Instant culling.** Opening a raw shows its embedded camera preview or cached render within ~0.1 s while the full render follows (~0.2–0.5 s for 24 MP). The next and previous photos are prepared in the background, so stepping through a shoot takes ~50 ms per photo. - **Background rendering.** A worker pool renders the loupe, before/after and every visible thumbnail off the UI thread: drafts during drags, full quality on release. - **Local-first.** No account, no cloud, no telemetry, no subscription. Your catalog is an append-only log of human-readable operations you can diff, back up or replay.
## Feature status LightCraft is young and moving fast: **alpha**. **Where we honestly stand** (details in the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) and [docs/target-app-parity.md](docs/target-app-parity.md)): - **By feature count we're at ~82%** (core features 98%), tracked row by row in [docs/parity-checklist.md](docs/parity-checklist.md). - **As a day-to-day tool we're nearer 61% for the whole product, ~51% for a typical working photographer and ~65% for casual use.** It's great for JPEG/DNG and most Sony / Panasonic / Fujifilm / Nikon / older-Canon raws on one machine; see [docs/raw-parity.md](docs/raw-parity.md) for your camera. - **The biggest gaps:** - **camera colour calibration:** Sony, Nikon, Panasonic, Fujifilm and Canon CR3 and CRW raws have guarded estimates from their camera JPEGs, with built-in Canon EOS D60, ILCA-99M2, ILCE-7CR, ILCE-7M4, ILCE-7RM5, X-H2S, X-T4, Nikon Z 6II, Z 8 and D5300 profiles; measured calibration covers one model so far (chart-measured matrices for the Canon EOS D60), and other raws or rejected fits retain a neutral matrix; - **unsupported CR3 variants and Nikon High Efficiency NEFs:** these use embedded JPEG previews when present. Olympus compressed ORF is unsupported for sensor decoding and uses embedded JPEG previews when available ([docs/orf-compression.md](docs/orf-compression.md)); Fujifilm lossless/lossy compressed RAF now decodes sensor data; [verification and existing-library reload instructions](docs/raf-compression.md); - **AI quality and model setup:** Subject and Sky selection are classical heuristics; Object/Describe use an optional SAM 3 model. AI Denoise supports Bayer RAW with separately installed weights, while X-Trans and linear-RGB denoise and Super Resolution remain missing; see [AI masks](docs/ai-masks.md) and [AI Denoise](docs/denoise.md); - **network libraries:** a preview reads the raw's header — or, for a CR3 or a TIFF raw whose preview tag sits past it, exactly the ranges the sparse planner names — and its embedded JPEG only (56.5 MB → 5.9 MB, 10 s → 1 s on the test share), but the *developed* picture still needs the sensor data over the wire; see [docs/raw-preview-reads.md](docs/raw-preview-reads.md); - **on-screen HDR display, video import/editing, and the Book / Map module views.** Print layouts and colour-managed PDF output work; direct printer output and page overlays remain missing. Slideshow playback and export work, with a dedicated module editor and music still missing. - **What's next:** see [the ranked gaps](docs/gaps.md) and [the roadmap](docs/roadmap.md). | Area | Status | |---|---| | Library: albums, folders, smart albums, stacks (incl. auto-stack), virtual copies, ratings, flags, labels, filter bar, search, sort, grids, filmstrip | ✅ | | Culling: Compare (synced zoom) and Survey views, auto-advance, instant previews | ✅ | | Light, Color, Effects (vignette styles), Tone Curve (+ refine saturation, targeted adjustment), Color Mixer (+ targeted), Point Color, Color Grading, Calibration, B&W | ✅ | | Masking: brush, linear, radial, luminance/colour range, add/subtract/intersect; Object and Describe selections | ✅ · Object/Describe require optional SAM 3; Subject/Sky remain heuristic ([details](docs/ai-masks.md)) | | Crop, straighten tool + auto straighten, flip, rotate, aspect ratios, overlays | ✅ | | Profiles (Color, Neutral, Vivid, Landscape, Portrait, Monochrome: our own looks), presets, versions, history, copy/paste/sync settings | ✅ | | Camera colour: DNG matrices, guarded camera-JPEG look fits and built-in profiles for selected cameras | 🚧 measured calibration and per-model coverage remain incomplete ([raw parity](docs/raw-parity.md)) | | Native macOS menu bar (generated from the command registry), control channel + every widget addressable, headless UI snapshots | ✅ | | RAW: DNG, CR2, CR3 (lossless CRX Bayer and version 0x100/0x200 C-RAW), ARW, NEF (uncompressed + lossless/lossy compressed, incl. lossy after split), Fujifilm RAF (uncompressed + lossless/lossy compressed, Bayer + X-Trans), Panasonic RW2 / Leica RWL / Panasonic RAW (every raw format, DMC-LX1 to DC-S1RM2), Pentax PEF, Olympus ORF (uncompressed, 12.8 bpp), Samsung SRW (uncompressed); embedded previews for every format incl. ## Quick start Workspace builds, including the desktop, web and CLI applications, require Rust 1.95 or newer. ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft && cd lightcraft cargo run --release -p lightcraft # opens your library (~/Pictures/LightCraft Library; a new one starts with demo photos) cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- ~/Pictures/trip # import your photos (folders are scanned, duplicates skipped) cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- --memory # a throwaway in-memory demo session (writes nothing) cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- --control 7980 # with the automation channel cargo xtask web --serve # the same app in the browser: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ cargo run --release -p lightcraft-cli -- render photo.jpg -o out.jpg --set light.exposure=0.5 cargo xtask ci # fmt, clippy, HEIF, tests, parity, layers, assets, WASM cargo xtask ci --quick # only what your branch's changes can break (minutes) ``` `cargo xtask ci --quick` compares with the merge base of `origin/main` (`--base REF` for another) and runs fmt, clippy, the tests of the changed packages, layers and assets, plus HEIF, parity and the wasm check when the changes touch them; a change to `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or the lint config tests everything. GitHub runs the full `cargo xtask ci` on every pull request (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Only one `ci` runs at a time per machine: a second one, from another worktree say, waits for the first and names it, since several at once take longer in total than in turn. `LIGHTCRAFT_CI_SLOTS=2` allows two; `LIGHTCRAFT_CI_LOCK=off` skips the lock. CI defaults to line-table debug information and one build job per 1.5 GB of RAM available when it starts (at most one per CPU; 4 if memory can't be read), so an 8 GB machine with 6 GB free builds with 4, and a busy machine with little free builds with fewer. Test threads follow, capped at 4. Full-debuginfo linkers, one per CPU, otherwise exhaust RAM before any test runs. GPU coverage is unchanged. Explicit `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, `RUST_TEST_THREADS` and `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS` settings override these defaults. The tests run under `cargo test`; `LIGHTCRAFT_NEXTEST=1` runs them under [cargo-nextest](https://nexte.st) instead (one process per test, slower here because each regenerates the demo scenes). Ordinary development commands keep their own settings. **Release builds on memory-constrained machines:** [#1196](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1196) reports Arch/AUR release-link OOM kills on a 16 GB machine when the desktop and CLI build concurrently with full debug information, thin LTO and one codegen unit. The CI defaults above do not apply to ordinary `cargo build --release`. Start with one job; two may be suitable if enough memory is available: ```sh CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli # Alternatively: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli ``` If a packaging environment enables full debug information or memory-heavy LTO settings, use command-local overrides for a lower-memory source build: ```sh CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli ``` These POSIX-shell assignments affect only this command, not global Cargo configuration or the repository's release profiles. Disabling LTO may change performance and binary size; disabling debug information reduces debugging detail. This is build guidance, not a guarantee that any machine has enough memory. Downstream packagers should serialize large binary builds and avoid full debug information combined with LTO and one codegen unit on low-memory builders. A PKGBUILD that exports its own profile settings can override inherited variables; adjust the packaging recipe locally or contact its maintainer rather than assuming an environment prefix on `makepkg` will take precedence. **Linux/Arch build troubleshooting: rustc SIGILL with ThinLTO.** In [#2811](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2811), an Arch Linux x86_64 build on an AMD Ryzen 9 7900X3D with 64 GB RAM failed with rustc 1.99.0 / LLVM 23.1.1, AUR `lightcraft` `0.7.1-1` and `0.13.0-1`, `RUSTFLAGS="-C opt-level=3 -C target-cpu=native"`, and release settings `opt-level=3`, `lto=thin`, `codegen-units=1`. `cargo build --frozen --release` reached the executable crates before rustc crashed with signal 4 (`SIGILL` / `ILL_ILLOPN`). The core dumps point into LLVM's SelectionDAG / vector-combine optimization path; the exact compiler root cause has not been isolated. This does not mean every machine with that hardware or toolchain will fail. It is a different observed failure from the 16 GB OOM kills in [#1196](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1196) above; there is no evidence establishing a shared root cause. For a direct Cargo source build, the equivalent command-local LTO override is: ```sh CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off cargo build --frozen --release ``` Reporter @rwarmstr verified the workaround by exporting `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off` **inside the AUR PKGBUILD's `_srcenv()` function** and rebuilding both package versions, without changing `RUSTFLAGS`. The reporter tested the AUR recipe, not the direct Cargo invocation above. A variable prefixed to `makepkg` alone may be overwritten by the PKGBUILD's own exports; the recipe must honor or set the override. The AUR `!lto` opt-out behavior is tracked separately in [#2813](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2813). [Cargo's LTO documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#lto) distinguishes `false` from `off`: `false` can still perform thin local LTO across codegen units (unless `codegen-units=1` or `opt-level=0`); `off` disables LTO explicitly. The low-memory recipe above is unchanged. This workaround is for affected builds, not a new default; disabling LTO may change performance, binary size and build behavior. Tests that need a GPU, the corpus, the craft-fonts faces or a model pass without checking anything when those are missing (libtest has no "skipped" status), so `cargo xtask ci` lists them: tests record a skip with `lightcraft_testkit::skip!`, and the run ends with what the machine offered (OS, CPUs, RAM, GPU adapters per backend, corpus, fonts) and every skip by reason. It writes `target/ci/report.json` and `target/ci/summary.md`, a block to paste into a PR (`--summary-md` prints it); `--hardware` also runs the GPU tests on every backend that has a hardware adapter. Nothing is uploaded. **Chinese and Japanese text** need the shared font repo, an optional build input (official releases always include it): ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts ../craft-fonts CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo run --release -p lightcraft ``` Without it LightCraft builds and runs the same, but Chinese and Japanese text have no glyphs. Fonts are never committed to this repo — what goes there is described in the [craft-fonts README](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts#readme). **Interface language:** **Edit → Language** (English, 简体中文, 繁體中文（台灣）, 日本語, Português (Brasil), Español, Deutsch, Русский, Français, Українська, Polski, Čeština, Italiano, ქართული, Svenska, Suomi, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt) or **Settings → General → Language**; the choice applies immediately and persists. See [docs/localization.md](docs/localization.md). **Logs:** the desktop app writes its log to standard error and to `logs/lightcraft.log` in its settings folder (Linux `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lightcraft/logs/`, by default `~/.config/lightcraft/logs/`; macOS `~/Library/Application Support/LightCraft/logs/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\LightCraft\logs\`), never in the library. **Portable mode:** a file named `portable.txt` (or `LightCraft.portable`) next to the executable moves the settings folder to `LightCraftData` beside it. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so attach this file to a bug report (**Help ▸ Open Log Folder** shows it in the file manager). Each start moves the previous log to `lightcraft.1.log` and that one to `lightcraft.2.log`, so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start; the file stops growing at 16 MiB, `--version` and `--help` write none, and runs with `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS` log to standard error only. By default LightCraft's own crates log at `info` and everything else at `warn`. `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG=info` or `debug` works as before (that level for LightCraft's own crates, warnings and errors from the rest; any other value: warnings and errors only) and wins over `RUST_LOG`, which otherwise replaces the default with env_logger-style directives such as `RUST_LOG=debug` or `RUST_LOG=warn,lightcraft_pipeline=trace` (a directive ending in `*` covers every target starting with it, as in `lightcraft*=debug`). Panics are recorded there too, and still in `lightcraft-panics.log` in the temp folder. The logger is `apps/lightcraft/src/logging.rs`. The web build needs the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target and the matching `wasm-bindgen` CLI (`cargo xtask web` prints the exact install command); see [docs/web.md](docs/web.md). **Nix** builds the desktop app and `lightcraft-cli` (the Nix build always includes the craft-fonts input, so Japanese text has glyphs): ```sh nix run github:storytold/lightcraft # the desktop app nix build github:storytold/lightcraft # → ./result/bin/{lightcraft,lightcraft-cli} nix develop github:storytold/lightcraft # rust toolchain + native deps + fonts ``` On NixOS, run a `cargo` build from `nix develop`: outside it the app can't find `libvulkan.so.1`, finds no GPU and renders on the CPU, much more slowly (it says so once at start-up). `nix run` and `nix build` set the path themselves. In a flake configuration (NixOS, home-manager, nix-darwin): ```nix # flake.nix inputs.lightcraft.url = "github:storytold/lightcraft"; # optional: build against your own nixpkgs instead of the one LightCraft pins # inputs.lightcraft.inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs"; # then, in a NixOS or home-manager module (where `inputs` is in scope): nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.lightcraft.overlays.default ]; # makes `pkgs.lightcraft` available environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.lightcraft ]; # home-manager: home.packages = [ pkgs.lightcraft ]; ``` `nix build` installs the same desktop file, hicolor icons and AppStream metadata as the .deb/.rpm, and runs `cargo test --workspace` as its check phase (skip it with `pkgs.lightcraft.overrideAttrs { doCheck = false; }`). **Keyboard:** G grid · D detail · E edit · C crop · M masking · Shift+P presets · \\ original · Y before/after · Z zoom · J clipping · ⌘Z undo · ⌘/ all shortcuts. ## How it's built An engine-first Cargo workspace of small, tested crates with enforced layering (`cargo xtask layers`): `geom`, `color`, `raster`, `tiff` → `raw`, `codecs`, `meta`, `develop` → `pipeline` → `catalog` → `engine` → `ui-egui`. The egui frontend is one swappable crate; nothing below it knows a UI exists. `mcp` and the apps (`lightcraft`, `lightcraft-cli`) sit on top of `engine`. ## Contributing Humans and agents follow the same rules, so read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) first. The short version: - **Clean-room.** Never read proprietary binaries or GPL raw/photo code (darktable, RawTherapee, LibRaw, rawspeed, dcraw…); work from public specs and black-box observation. - **No proprietary assets, ever:** no icons, screenshots, presets, profiles, LUTs or fonts from commercial products. Every image, icon and font in the repo is original, public domain, Creative Commons, OFL or permissively licensed, and has an entry in [assets/ATTRIBUTION.md](assets/ATTRIBUTION.md) added in the same commit. New fonts go to [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts), not here. - **Pure Rust**, enforced crate layering, everything is a command, and `cargo xtask ci` green before every commit (one task id per commit). - **Never crash.** Non-test code returns errors instead of panicking: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!` or `unsafe`, checked indexing on anything derived from input, and a regression test with every crash fix. Details in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#never-crash-outranks-feature-work). Questions, ideas or a bug you'd like to talk through first? Bring them to [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).
## Downloads **New to LightCraft?** Download it from the [LightCraft page on getartcraft.com](https://getartcraft.com/apps/lightcraft). That's the easiest way to install it. **Want a specific build or format?** On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `lightcraft--windows-x64.msi` | `lightcraft--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `lightcraft--windows-arm64.msi` | `lightcraft--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `lightcraft--windows-x86.msi` | `lightcraft--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The installer asks who to install for and where (for your account only, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\LightCraft`, by default; "Everyone on this computer" uses `C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\LightCraft` (`Program Files (x86)` for the 32-bit build); upgrades stay in the folder you chose) and ends on a page confirming LightCraft was installed, with an option to start it. For unattended installs: `msiexec /i lightcraft--windows-x64.msi /qn INSTALLFOLDER="D:\Apps\LightCraft\"`. A silent install is per-user by default. `INSTALLFOLDER` chooses the folder, not who it is installed for; add `ALLUSERS=1`, from an elevated terminal or deployment tool, for an all-users install. **Update or uninstall asks for an old `.msi`, or stops with error 1612 or 1714?** Windows removes the installed version with its own cached copy of that version's installer; if the copy is gone, it asks for the original file and stops (an update then ends with error 1603). Download the release MSI of the version and build you have installed from [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/releases) and run `msiexec /fv "" /qb+ /norestart`, approving the permission prompt if Windows shows one. That restores the cached copy; then retry the update or uninstall. Opening the MSI, or choosing Repair or Uninstall on it, may still fail. Error 1603 has other causes too; if this doesn't help, open an issue with the error message. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `lightcraft--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `lightcraft-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized | ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `lightcraft--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `lightcraft--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Portable; updates with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `lightcraft--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `lightcraft--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed; `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `lightcraft--linux-x86_64.deb` | `lightcraft--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `lightcraft--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `lightcraft--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `lightcraft--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `lightcraft--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `lightcraft--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only (glibc 2.39 or newer, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04+). On a Wayland desktop LightCraft runs through XWayland when it is available, because only X11 gives windows file drag-and-drop; set `LIGHTCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` to use native Wayland (sharper fractional scaling, no drop). ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `lightcraft--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Static site | `lightcraft-web-.zip` | Runs in a modern browser; host it on any static server |
